subject: science
question_text: Why does an athlete breathe faster and deeper than usual after finishing the race?
answer_text: An athlete needs to supply extra energy to his muscle cells which have worked hard during running. For this, he breathes faster and deeper so that more oxygen is supplied to the cells. This speeds up the breakdown of food and as a result, more energy is released.
final_answer: Thus, the athlete breathes faster and deeper to meet the increased energy demand.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of energy needs during physical exertion.

subject: science
question_text: List the similarities and differences between aerobic and anaerobic respiration.
answer_text:
Similarity: In both aerobic and anaerobic respiration, the food is broken down to release energy.
Differences:
Aerobic respiration occurs in the presence of oxygen, while anaerobic respiration occurs in the absence of oxygen. Aerobic respiration produces carbon dioxide and water, while anaerobic respiration produces lactic acid or alcohol. Aerobic respiration takes longer to release energy, whereas anaerobic respiration is faster. Aerobic respiration produces a large amount of energy, while anaerobic respiration produces a small amount.
final_answer: In summary, aerobic respiration is more efficient and occurs with oxygen, while anaerobic respiration is quicker and occurs without oxygen.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of both processes and their differences.

subject: science
question_text: Why do we often sneeze when we inhale a lot of dust-laden air?
answer_text: Sneezing expels the foreign particles from the inhaled air, so that only clean air enters our body. It usually occurs because of the irritation in the upper breathing passage when we inhale unwanted particles that get trapped in our nasal cavity.
final_answer: Therefore, sneezing helps to clear the nasal passage of irritants.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves basic understanding of respiratory responses to irritants.

subject: science
question_text: Which test-tube would have the highest concentration of CO₂?
answer_text: Test tube A will have the highest concentration of CO₂ because it contains a snail, which breathes in O₂ and breathes out CO₂. Test tube B contains a water plant that takes in CO₂ for food synthesis and gives out O₂. Test tube C contains both a snail and a plant, where the CO₂ produced by the snail is utilized by the plant.
final_answer: Therefore, test tube A has the highest concentration of CO₂.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of the interactions between organisms and gas exchange.

question_text:
The mountaineers carry oxygen with them because:
(a) At an altitude of more than 5 km there is no air.
(b) The amount of air available to a person is less than that available on the ground.
(c) The temperature of air is higher than that on the ground.
(d) The pressure of air is higher than that on the ground.

mcq_options.option_text: At an altitude of more than 5 km there is no air.
The amount of air available to a person is less than that available on the ground.
The temperature of air is higher than that on the ground.
The pressure of air is higher than that on the ground.

answer_text: The mountaineers carry oxygen with them because the amount of air available to a person is less than that available on the ground.
final_answer: Therefore, mountaineers carry oxygen due to lower air availability at high altitudes.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of atmospheric conditions at high altitudes.
